Item 3 of the recommendation that closed the islands brainstorm (dec:idea-a-claimed-blast-radius-is-an-island-no-other-session-writes-in).","statement":"Every agent working a design can present its own identity on every call. That includes each session, each subagent inside a session, and each caller behind a hosting gateway. Claims, write warnings and any "who is working where" view use that identity, so any two agents are distinct, even when they act for the same person.

- A claim is held by the agent that made it. A second agent's claim on the same ground stands beside the first and never silently replaces it.
- Overlap between two agents' claims is reported even when both act for the same person.

WHY (measured 2026-09-29, fact:a-claim-cannot-tell-two-agents-of-one-person-apart-and-on-flo2-io-not-even-two-people-2026-09-29):
- Claims are keyed by (contributor, seed), so a second claim on the same seed replaces the first.
- claim_report skips same-contributor overlaps: today's three parallel fix agents overlap by up to 77 nodes and nothing reports it.
- Subagents share their parent's seat.
- On flo2.io every caller to a design shares one engine seat.
- The concurrency that actually happens is one person's parallel subagents (up to 10 writers in 10 minutes), which is exactly the case this cannot see today.

This extends req:seat-per-client (accepted: "who is working is a property of the session") down to subagents and across the hosting gateway. flo2's half, carrying each caller's identity through the gateway, is flo2's req:the-gateway-gives-each-calling-agent-its-own-seat. The seat still going `gone` while its agent works is a separate defect with its own record (req:a-claim-reads-gone-only-when-the-server-holding-its-session-saw-it-end and its root cause); this needs that fixed too. Identity serves coordination and attribution, never authority (req:a-write-and-an-approval-record-the-agent-and-the-person-it-acts-for).","status":"accepted"}
